_doc: This file IS the policy: no jurisdictional 'if' may exist anywhere else in the codebase.
Changing it changes what the product is legally allowed to do, so it is reviewed like code
and its version + hash are recorded in PolicyChangeLog on deploy.
Fail-closed by construction: default_state is 'disabled' for every feature, and a
jurisdiction that is absent from a feature's jurisdiction_policy falls back to it.
An unregistered feature key is denied outright.
verified_sources: only these may LOWER strictness (§6.2). A self-declared or inferred
jurisdiction can make the profile stricter, never looser.

cmf_attention.legal_basis_ref: RND_01_JURISDICTION.md — matrix row (a); RU: 152-FZ art. 11 (no identity establishment => not biometric PD); EU: AI Act art. 5(1)(f) + Guidelines C(2025) 884 cl. 255 (inferring interest and attention of students is prohibited; on-device processing does not cure it)
cmf_attention.note: Covers the on-device attention pipeline AND its per-bucket aggregate ingress. EU stays disabled: the output functions as 'attention', which cl. 248 anti-circumvention blocks from being renamed out of scope.

selfreport_state.legal_basis_ref: RND_01_JURISDICTION.md — matrix row (b); AI Act art. 3(39) requires inference from biometric data, a self-report is not; Guidelines cl. 251/265 place it out of scope. EU conditions: GDPR art. 9 + art. 8 consent, DPIA, and NO fusion with the camera module.
selfreport_state.note: The primary EU-legal path to the same product value. Enabled in both regimes; still disabled under an unknown jurisdiction, because an unmodelled third regime is not a known-safe one.

recommend_schedule.legal_basis_ref: RND_01_JURISDICTION.md — matrix row (g); EU: with a camera-derived input the recommendation inherits the art. 5(1)(f) prohibition, and on a self-report input it is likely Annex III 3(b) high-risk with the art. 6(3) profiling filter blocked.
recommend_schedule.note: A future EU variant fed strictly by self-report + explicit preferences must be registered as its own feature key, not smuggled in under this one.

ubp_profile.legal_basis_ref: RND_01_JURISDICTION.md — matrix row (d); EU: UBP is textbook profiling (GDPR art. 4(4)), and if it steers level or track it lands in Annex III 3(c) => always high-risk under art. 6(3). RU: ordinary personal data, subject to localisation.
ubp_profile.note: IndexedDB storage does not change the analysis — the rule is about the function, not the storage location.

face_emotion_recognition.legal_basis_ref: RND_01_JURISDICTION.md — matrix row (c) and red line 2; EU: prohibited unconditionally, consent cannot cure it (up to EUR 35M / 7%). RU: legally arguable but a reputational red line the product does not cross.
face_emotion_recognition.note: Registered precisely because it is never to be built: the matrix is the machine-checkable form of that red line, so any future call site fails closed instead of quietly working.

peer_chat.legal_basis_ref: Owner decision 2026-08-13 (PROMPT_13 §6.3): the platform ships OPEN. Laws move in both directions, so we do not guess at a region's rule in advance and we do not pre-emptively restrict — a restriction is introduced only when we actually enter a region and know the norm it requires. Enabled in every modelled jurisdiction; an UNMODELLED one still fails closed by construction, which is the property this matrix exists to guarantee.
peer_chat.note: Enabling a region is an edit to THIS file; so is restricting one, and that needs an owner decision naming the region and the norm. The stricter mechanisms (permanent visibility, pre-moderation, stop-words, no direct messages) remain in InstitutionChatSettings, all OFF — they are where a region's rule will land, not something to switch on by analogy.

lesson_summary.legal_basis_ref: PROMPT_13 §5 (owner decision 2026-08-12, §4.2 п.1). The summary is assembled from material the platform already stores lawfully — the lesson plan, the board, the test results and the lesson chat — and is shared only with the people who were in the lesson. No biometric or speech input is involved on this key: EU stays enabled precisely because the EU path is 'summary without transcription', which is this feature minus lesson_transcription.
lesson_summary.note: Two keys, deliberately. A regime that forbids processing lesson speech does not thereby forbid writing down what was on the board — collapsing them into one switch would have cost the EU the whole feature.

lesson_transcription.legal_basis_ref: PROMPT_13 §5 and §4.1. RU: 152-FZ processing of ordinary personal data with the speaker's explicit consent (a minor's via the guardian's art. 9 consent, the existing consent152fz), no storage of audio or of a verbatim transcript. EU: disabled — processing pupils' speech in a classroom is systematic monitoring of minors under GDPR art. 8 + art. 35(3)(b), and the DPIA and legal basis for it have not been established; the summary is still produced there, from the board, the test and the chat.
lesson_transcription.note: The gate covers deriving summary points from speech. It does NOT authorise storing audio or a transcript — that is forbidden everywhere by §4.1, in every jurisdiction, and is not a matrix question. Speech lives in process memory only (apps/summaries/speech_stream.py) and is dropped at assembly; a speaker's own consent is checked on top of this key, per speaker (apps/summaries/consent.py).
